title: Tradeweb Exchange-Traded Funds Update – October 2026
summary: Trading activity on the Tradeweb European ETF marketplace reached EUR 74.9 billion in October, an increase of 3% year-over-year. Transactions completed via Tradeweb’s Automated Intelligent Execution (AiEX) tool accounted for 96% of tickets and a record 37% of notional volume.
body_markdown:
The following data is derived from trading activity on the Tradeweb Markets institutional European- and U.S.-listed ETF platforms.


#### EUROPEAN-LISTED ETFs


**Total traded volume**


Trading activity on the Tradeweb European ETF marketplace reached EUR 74.9 billion in October, an increase of 3% year-over-year. Transactions completed via Tradeweb’s Automated Intelligent Execution (AiEX) tool accounted for 96% of tickets and a record 37% of notional volume.


Adam Gould, Global Head of Equities at Tradeweb, said: “European ETF activity rose in October, with net buying across equity and fixed income products. The range of exposures traded shows how institutions use ETFs to manage their portfolios, while AiEX’s record share of notional volume highlights the growing role of rules-based automation in their workflows.”


**Volume breakdown**


In contrast to equity and fixed income ETFs, commodity products saw net selling in October. Activity in the asset class dropped to 4% of the total platform flow, half their share of the previous 12-month rolling average. The proportion of stock- and bond-based ETF volume on the platform amounted to 72% and 24%, respectively.


Meanwhile, North America Equities overtook Global Equities as the most heavily-traded ETF category during the month, with EUR 20 billion in total traded volume. Government bonds recorded the highest buy ratio among the top five categories at 62%, narrowly ahead of Global Equities at 61%.


**Top ten by traded notional volume**


The iShares Core S&P 500 UCITS ETF took the lead in October’s top ten list, after its previous appearance in August 2026. Slipping one spot from September, the iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF was ranked second. In fourth place, the iShares Core Corporate Bond UCITS ETF was the only fixed income fund to feature in the top ten.


#### U.S.-LISTED ETFs


**Total traded volume**


Total consolidated U.S. ETF notional value traded in October was a record USD 134.6 billion, up 50% year-over-year. The proportion of AiEX transactions and notional volume amounted to 57% and 17%, respectively.


Adam Gould, Global Head of Equities at Tradeweb, said: “October’s technology sell-off, rising oil prices, and broad government bond rally gave investors plenty to respond to. Against this backdrop, trading on our U.S. ETF platform reached a record high, as clients adjusted exposures across equity and fixed income markets.”


**Volume breakdown**


As a percentage of total notional value traded, equities accounted for 55% and fixed income for 41%, with the remainder comprising commodity and specialty ETFs.


**Top ten by traded notional volume**


The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF proved to be the most actively-traded product for the 12th consecutive month. The iShares Russell 1000 Growth ETF was ranked second, while the iShares National Muni Bond ETF moved up two places from September to take the third spot.
